title: Microsoft's Big Outage Leaves Millions Unable to Email
summary:
On Thursday evening, something big went wrong at Microsoft. People in 74 countries suddenly found they could not use Outlook, the email service used by millions around the world. Many could not send or receive emails, open files, or check their calendars.

The trouble spread beyond email. Microsoft 365, the package that includes Teams, Outlook and the artificial intelligence helper Copilot, was hit by what Microsoft called 'connectivity problems'. Some people could still chat and join online meetings on Teams, while others were locked out completely.

The scale is hard to pin down. More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, according to Microsoft's own website. The monitoring site Downdetector counted 140,000 people reporting Outlook problems on Thursday evening, but the real number is probably much higher, since it only counts people who report a problem.

The outage reached far beyond home computers. The trouble spilled over to other services too. OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, said some of its tools were not working as expected. Anthropic reported problems too. Government offices were affected as well, including the Singaporean government and Australia's spy agency. In the UK, GP surgeries, pharmacies, police and schools felt the impact. Some surgeries asked patients not to send messages through their websites, and several large police forces asked people to phone in reports instead.

Microsoft has ruled out a cyber-attack. It blames 'elevated load' — in plain terms, its servers were under far more strain than usual. A large number of servers became 'unexpectedly unavailable', the company said, and the extra traffic strained the servers that were left.

By Friday morning, Microsoft said it was seeing 'early signs of stabilisation', but service capacity had 'not yet returned to normal levels'. Fixing the problem was not going as expected, and engineers were still working on it.
why_it_matters: When a service used by more than 430 million people stops working, emails, meetings, doctors' surgeries, police and schools can all be disrupted at once, showing how much everyday life depends on a small number of large technology systems.

keywords.explanation: An outage is when a service suddenly stops working for a lot of people at once.
Connectivity is about whether computers and services can link up and talk to each other over the internet.
A cyber-attack is when someone deliberately breaks into or disrupts computer systems on purpose.
Elevated load means the servers were being asked to handle far more work than usual.
Servers are powerful computers that run services like email and store the data they need.
Stabilisation means things are starting to calm down and work properly again after a problem.

background_read: Microsoft 365 is a set of online tools that many people use for work and school, including email, chat, video meetings and documents. Outlook is the email part of that set, and it works because messages are sent, stored and delivered by powerful computers called servers, which people reach over the internet. When many people use these tools at the same time, the servers have to handle a huge amount of traffic, so if some servers stop working, the ones that are left can become overloaded. That is what happened here: too many servers became unavailable at once, and the extra strain left many people unable to send or receive email or use the other tools.
